requirements.quote: Domain names in messages are expressed in terms of a sequence of labels.
requirements.condition: When representing a domain name in a message.
requirements.required_behavior: Express the domain name as a sequence of labels.
requirements.why_checkable: The message name representation can be inspected for its label sequence structure.

requirements.quote:
Each label is represented as a one octet length field followed by that
number of octets.
requirements.condition: When encoding a label in a domain name in a message.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the label length in a one-octet field.
requirements.why_checkable: The label length field width can be checked in the encoded message and serializer.

requirements.quote:
Each label is represented as a one octet length field followed by that
number of octets.
requirements.condition: When encoding a label in a domain name in a message.
requirements.required_behavior: Place exactly the number of label octets specified by the length field immediately after that field.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared length can be compared with the following label payload and its location.

requirements.quote:
Since every domain name ends with the null label of
the root, a domain name is terminated by a length byte of zero.
requirements.condition: When representing a domain name as a sequence of labels in a message.
requirements.required_behavior: Terminate the domain name with the root null label, represented by a zero length byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The final label length byte can be inspected for the zero value.

requirements.quote:
The
high order two bits of every length octet must be zero, and the
remaining six bits of the length field limit the label to 63 octets or
less.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the two high-order bits of the length octet to zero.
requirements.why_checkable: A bit-mask check on a label length octet directly verifies the required zero bits.

requirements.quote:
The
high order two bits of every length octet must be zero, and the
remaining six bits of the length field limit the label to 63 octets or
less.
requirements.condition: For the length of a label.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit label content to at most 63 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The label payload length can be checked against the 63-octet upper bound.

requirements.quote:
To simplify implementations, the total length of a domain name (i.e.,
label octets and label length octets) is restricted to 255 octets or
less.
requirements.condition: When measuring the total length of a domain name.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the combined number of label octets and label length octets to at most 255.
requirements.why_checkable: The sum of all label payload and label length octets can be checked at the 255-octet boundary.

requirements.quote:
Although labels can contain any 8 bit values in octets that make up a
label,
requirements.condition: For the permitted values of octets within a label.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit any 8-bit value in a label content octet.
requirements.why_checkable: Label-content representation and validation can be checked across all 256 octet values.

requirements.quote:
Although labels can contain any 8 bit values in octets that make up a
label, it is strongly recommended that labels follow the preferred
syntax described elsewhere in this memo, which is compatible with
existing host naming conventions.
requirements.required_behavior: Strongly prefer the recommended label syntax described elsewhere in the memo; this is advisory rather than mandatory.
requirements.why_checkable: The syntax recommendation refers to rules absent from this chunk, so the exact implementation check cannot be established from this evidence alone.

requirements.quote:
Name servers and resolvers must
compare labels in a case-insensitive manner (i.e., A=a), assuming ASCII
with zero parity.
requirements.condition: When a name server or resolver compares labels, assuming ASCII with zero parity.
requirements.required_behavior: Compare alphabetic label characters without distinguishing uppercase and lowercase.
requirements.why_checkable: Label comparison can be exercised with corresponding uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters.

requirements.quote:
Name servers and resolvers must
compare labels in a case-insensitive manner (i.e., A=a), assuming ASCII
with zero parity.  Non-alphabetic codes must match exactly.
requirements.condition: When a name server or resolver compares non-alphabetic codes in labels, assuming ASCII with zero parity.
requirements.required_behavior: Require exact equality of non-alphabetic codes for those codes to match.
requirements.why_checkable: Comparisons of equal and unequal non-alphabetic codes directly expose exact-match behavior.
